articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
This amendment updates existing authorizations concerning transactions related to Iran, reflecting ongoing adjustments to the U.S. sanctions policy towards the country.
Further details regarding the scope and implications of this amended general license are available on the Treasury's website.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Related to North Korea and DRC
body: On October 28, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

The North Korea-related designations target individuals and one entity for their roles in government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes that defraud American businesses and generate revenue for Pyongyang's weapons programs. These schemes utilize fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas to secure employment with legitimate companies, including those in the United States.

The action against North Korea follows broader international efforts to disrupt the DPRK's ability to fund its unlawful development of weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missiles, and to counter unlawful DPRK-Russia military cooperation. The DRC-related designations were also announced on this date, though specific details of these designations were not immediately available in the initial OFAC release.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement Agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc.
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) reached a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026.
This settlement addresses alleged violations of OFAC sanctions regulations by the company.
Further details of the settlement, including the specific violations and the agreed-upon penalty, are outlined in the official OFAC announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, concerning the blocking and rejecting of transactions and the filing of reports with OFAC.
These amendments aim to provide updated guidance and clarification for individuals and entities subject to OFAC regulations.
The revised FAQs are intended to assist in compliance efforts and ensure proper reporting procedures are followed.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting persons and vessels supporting Iran's shadow fleet and trade in petroleum, petrochemicals, and other commodities. This action notably includes the designation of a Panama- and Greece-based law firm, Karnakis and Karnakis, five individuals associated with the firm, and shipping companies and agents, along with the identification of several vessels as blocked property.
Concurrently, OFAC announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions in these areas.

The Treasury Department also issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions, providing authorizations for certain wind-down, safety, environmental, and cargo-related transactions involving the newly blocked persons and property.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State / Holland & Knight

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities involved in activities that undermine American intellectual property rights.
Associated General Licenses were also issued to provide guidance and authorizations related to these new designations.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related and Cuba-Related Entities; Issues New General Licenses

These actions are part of ongoing efforts to address activities deemed contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests in both regions.
In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions to provide guidance on permissible transactions and activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: On October 13, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new designations under its Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism sanctions programs.
These actions target individuals and entities involved in illicit narcotics trafficking and terrorism-related activities.
The designations aim to disrupt financial networks and support systems for these illicit operations globally.

articles.headline: EU Adopts Largest-Ever Russia Sanctions Package Targeting Military-Industrial Complex
body: On October 12, 2026, the Council of the European Union adopted its largest package of Russia-related listings to date, imposing restrictive measures on 1,569 individuals and entities within Russia's military-industrial complex.

This 22nd package of sanctions targets 826 Russian companies supplying components for missiles, UAVs, and aircraft, as well as 743 individuals serving as CEOs of these companies. The targeted companies reportedly have a combined annual turnover of at least €20 billion and employ over 250,000 people.

Additionally, the Council listed 77 individuals in connection with the September 2026 Russian State Duma elections held in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine, and on October 15, imposed restrictive measures on three individuals and nine entities involved in circumventing EU sanctions.
articles.source: Council of the European Union / Squire Patton Boggs / This Month in EU Sanctions

articles.headline: EU Adds Individuals and Entities to DPRK Sanctions List Over Nuclear Programs and Russia Ties
body: The Council of the European Union adopted additional restrictive measures against three individuals and four entities under its autonomous sanctions list on the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) on October 12, 2026.

These designations target those responsible for supporting, promoting, or facilitating activities contributing to the DPRK's nuclear weapons, ballistic missile, or other weapons of mass destruction programs, as well as for violating and evading United Nations sanctions.

The new listings specifically address activities linked to the growing military and economic cooperation between the DPRK and Russia, including the deployment of DPRK workers in Russia, commercial and industrial cooperation, and the 'arms-for-oil' trade, all in violation of UN Security Council prohibitions.

articles.headline: UN General Assembly Condemns US Embargo on Cuba for 34th Consecutive Year
body: The United Nations General Assembly overwhelmingly passed a resolution on October 28, 2026, condemning the decades-long U.S. economic, commercial, and financial embargo against Cuba for the 34th consecutive year.

The resolution, which calls for an end to the blockade, was adopted with 130 votes in favor, 17 against, and 25 abstentions. This marks a notable decrease in support compared to the previous year, when over 160 nations supported the measure.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla blamed the embargo for strangling Cuba's health system, citing a doubling of infant mortality and delays in tens of thousands of surgeries. The U.S. representative, Mike Waltz, countered that there is no blockade and accused the military-run business monopoly of hoarding resources.
articles.source: UN News / China Daily HK / PBS News

articles.headline: OFAC Alerts Foreign Financial Institutions to Iran Sanctions Risk Under 'Operation Economic Outcast'
body: On October 5, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an alert to foreign financial institutions, warning that continued business with Iran or its financial sector could lead to sanctions under 'Operation Economic Outcast.'

OFAC emphasized that foreign financial institutions transacting with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions risk being targeted without advance notification and should immediately terminate such activities and relationships.

This alert follows Treasury's expansion of secondary sanctions risk under Executive Order 13902 in August 2026, targeting individuals and entities supporting Iran's digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping sectors.

articles.headline: US Inflation Accelerates to 3.7% in September, Raising Concerns Ahead of Midterms
body: U.S. inflation accelerated in September, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising to an annualized rate of 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August, according to new data released on October 29, 2026.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, also showed prices increasing 0.5% for the month in September, with the annualized rate rising to 3.6% from 3.4% in August.

Rising gasoline prices, driven by renewed violence in the Middle East keeping oil prices above $100 a barrel, were a major contributor to the increase. However, prices for services such as shipping, hotel rooms, and utilities also increased rapidly, indicating that inflation is broadening and becoming more entrenched.

articles.headline: Eurozone Inflation Shows Mixed Trends in October; Italy and France See Increases
body: Inflation data released on October 30, 2026, for the eurozone's four largest economies revealed mixed trends for October.

Italy experienced the highest price increase, with inflation reaching 5.4% year-over-year, primarily driven by a 31.4% surge in energy prices. France followed with a 3.4% increase, while Spain's inflation held steady at 4.9%.

Germany was an exception, with inflation dropping to 2.8% from 3.3%, largely due to a temporary cut in fuel taxes that took effect on October 1. Economists warn that this relief may be short-lived if fuel duties rise again in January and February.

body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released enforcement actions for October 2026, including significant penalties against American Express National Bank and Bank of America, National Association.

American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah, received a Cease and Desist Order and a $750 million civil money penalty for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports (SARs), and customer due diligence and customer identification program violations.

Bank of America, National Association, Charlotte, North Carolina, was assessed a $750 million civil money penalty for similar deficiencies in its BSA compliance program, failure to timely file SARs, and sending wires with inaccurate transmittor name information.

articles.headline: DHS Updates Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List with New Additions
body: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), as Chair of the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force (FLETF), announced the publication of an updated Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List on October 29, 2026.

This update adds three new entities to the UFLPA Entity List under Section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii), which identifies entities working with the government of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region to recruit, transport, transfer, harbor, or receive forced labor or members of persecuted groups out of Xinjiang.

The newly added entities are Baoding LYSZD Trade And Business Co., Ltd., Hetian Haolin Hair Accessories Co. Ltd. (and two aliases), and Hetian Taida Apparel Co., Ltd (and one alias). This action supersedes the UFLPA Entity List published in the Federal Register on August 3, 2026.
articles.source: Federal Register / U.S. Department of Homeland Security

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
